item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 101720
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located well northwest of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Storm Norbert, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well South-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms located well to the
south-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands are associated with a broad
trough of low pressure. Some gradual development of this system is
possible late this week and into the weekend while it moves
generally northward and then meanders to the southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

Central Portion and West Portion of the East Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure are located several hundred miles southwest of the
southwestern Mexico coast. Gradual development of this system is
expected, and a tropical depression is likely to form by early next
week while it moves generally west-northwestward over central and
western portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Norbert are issued under WMO
header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Norbert are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 102045
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026
 
...NORBERT STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY AS IT CONTINUES MOVING WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.5N 120.5W
ABOUT 820 MI...1315 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 16.5 North, longitude 120.5 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue through Friday. A turn toward the
west-northwest is forecast by Friday night.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) with
higher gusts. Gradual strengthening is forecast over the next few
days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 102046
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026
 
Norbert's structure can be described as a shear pattern, with the
low-level center near the western edge of the main convective area,
which has persisted for a while with very cold cloud tops.  The
TAFB intensity estimate is still 35 kt, but the objective estimates
have creeped up slightly, now in the 37-42 kt range.  Based on
those estimates, and the persistent nature of the deep convection,
the initial intensity estimate has been increased to 40 kt.
 
The tropical storm is moving westward, or 270/12 kt.  A
well-established mid-level ridge to the north of Norbert should keep
the cyclone moving in a direction between westward and
west-northwestward for the next several days.  The NHC track
forecast is slightly faster toward the west than the previous
official forecast and closely follows the latest HFIP Corrected
Consensus model (HCCA).
 
The sheared structure of Norbert and the proximity of drier air to 
the west of the system suggests that only modest near-term 
strengthening should be expected.  However, the shear is forecast to 
weaken over the next 24 hours, and SHIPS guidance forecasts 
mid-level relative humidity values between 60 and 70 percent, which 
are sufficiently moist enough for strengthening.  Most of the model 
guidance does not show a large amount of strengthening and keeps 
Norbert at tropical storm strength through the next 5 days. The 
Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean, HCCA, and COAMPS-TC models peak 
Norbert as a Category 1 hurricane in about 3 days before bringing it 
back down to tropical storm strength by day 4 with continued 
weakening into day 5.  The new NHC forecast brings Norbert up to 65 
kt by day 3, following the above models, and is higher than all of 
the available intensity guidance at days 4 and 5.  Given the spread 
in the guidance, the confidence in the intensity forecast is below 
average.
